So, the description. So, what you do is you provide a service for free that you can monetize another way. So, this works for one-time services or even recurring services, provided the recurring stream is high enough margins to pay for both. Different way of saying it, essentially, I give you thing A for free in exchange for buying thing B. Or I give you thing A for free, and I will encourage you to buy thing B. Or I give you a thing for free, as long as you continue to use thing B. Any of those things. So, the earmuff thing, he says, "I will give you these free earmuffs, and I will encourage you to store it." That's what that was, a classic upsell. So, if we have a lemonade stand with our classic upsell, we say we want to give you a free cup of lemonade. Upsell one might be, "Do you want, uh, lemonade ice cubes to make it cold without diluting it?" Now, of course, you could give cold lemonade, but then you wouldn't have an ice cube upsell. Upsell two would be, "Do you want a stainless steel to-go container to keep it cold for you? And we'll donate $1 to help children's cancer to anyone who takes the mug. You also get 20% off refills." Upsell number two. Right? So, you don't want lemonade in a little paper cup. You want a nice steel mug. You don't want diluted-down lemonade. You want lemonade ice cubes, right? Each of these things are just natural upsells that could happen, and I prove this point because whatever it is you sell, there's an upsell that's available for you. All right?
